page: Amazon Web Services i8g.8xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz on the arm64 architecture, eliminating hyperthreading contention. The compute configuration is paired with 256.0 GB of memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core, along with an integrated 7,500 GB NVMe SSD and a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No dedicated GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional memory and multi-core throughput. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 406.47 GB/sec, and write bandwidth hits 183.77 GB/sec, placing the instance in the top 10 percent of recorded systems. The PassMark memory score and Geekbench multi-core score (21,629.0) similarly hit top-tier levels. Database operations in PassMark reached 47,278.09, and Redis SET operations logged 67.73 million operations per second, supported by strong decompressive and code compilation throughput.

Tradeoffs emerge in single-threaded computing and large-scale model inference. Single-core stress-ng (1,707.1) and Geekbench single-core performance (1,886.0) align with mid-range baselines, and prompt processing for large 70B parameter language models falls into the bottom 25 percent at 5.91 tokens per second. Additionally, arm64 instruction set compatibility must be factored in for legacy software.

The dense NVMe storage volume, expansive RAM pool, and top-tier transactional memory efficiency deliver strong resource density for demanding data platforms. The i8g.8xlarge is primarily suited for high-throughput relational and NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, real-time analytics engines, and high-volume caching workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services i8g.8xlarge is a storage-optimized server utilizing the AWS Nitro System and arm64-based AWS Neoverse-V2 architecture. It provides 32 dedicated physical cores (32 vCPUs) clocked at 2.8 GHz, 256.0 GB of RAM, and 7,500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, supplemented by a 25 Gbps network baseline. Synthetic testing displays top-tier memory bandwidth (406.47 GB/sec read, 183.77 GB/sec write) and exceptional database operational throughput alongside a high Geekbench multi-core score of 21,629.0. However, single-core metrics sit in the middle 50 percent, and prompt execution speeds for large LLMs are limited. Delivering high memory density and massive local IO capacity per core, the i8g.8xlarge is well tailored for enterprise database operations, transactional key-value data stores, and large-scale analytical data processing.
